subject: geomorph - appending a list of factors to gpagen output

messages.author: 544eca9c804a0347
messages.subject: geomorph - appending a list of factors to gpagen output
parts:
Dear colleagues,

as this question is unrelated to the previous question about how to conduct a CVA, I decided to open it as a separate question.

I read in my files from a *.tps file into R using the function "readland.tps".
Then, with "gpagen", I am conducting a GPA and saved it as "y.gpa".
Now I am wondering how do I append my "group scheme", i.e. a single column that contains the "grouping variable/factor" to the output of "gpagen". My main issue seems to be that the "gpagen" output transposes the original data, so a simple "paste" such as

names(y.gpa) <- paste(grpreal$V1, seq_along(y.gpa), sep = "")

does not work and errors out with
ERROR:
'names' attribute [14000] must be the same length as the vector [15]

Might anyone be able to help out? Any help would be appreciated! Thank you in advance!

Cheers
Bob

messages.author: f16866fc42d43e64
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] geomorph - appending a list of factors to gpagen output
parts:
Bob, 

not sure what you would want to append a column of groups to the result of gpagen for, but in technical terms, the output of gpagen is a list, so to append anything to it you would do something like y.gpa$mygroups <- paste(grpreal$V1, seq_along(y.gpa), sep = "")

If your objective is to run an analysis that encompasses comparisons of groups within geomorph, like through procD.lm, the best approach would be to compile your shape (superimposed coordinates), CS (both pieces of the gpagen object), and group information (or any other variable of interest) into a geomorp.data.frame object. For this, please see the help file of geomorph.data.frame function.

Hope this helps
Antigoni
